ana: Heads-up: saw a reproducible mid-batch latency spike in prod yesterday ~22:14 UTC. nsight sys + perfetto traces attached to the run. Short summary: cublasLt probe picks an algo with large workspace, runtime tries cudaMallocAsync -> fragmentation -> fallback to a slower algo, plus concurrent KV cache evictions during the same window.

raj: :eyes: can you paste the nsys timeline slice? which kernels are hot?

ana: pasted snippet below (trimmed). notice repeated cudaMallocAsync stalls and alternating cublasLtMatmulAlgoX then cublasGemmEx fallback.
```
# nsys timeline excerpt
Kernel cublasLtMatmulAlgo3    412us
cudaMallocAsync              2.1ms  <-- stalls
Kernel cublasLtMatmulAlgo3    390us
Kernel cublasGemmEx          1.6ms  <-- fallback slow
KVCache::evict               120us  <-- many evicts
```

jun: interesting - so probe returns algo3 but workspace>slab. our allocator falls back to async malloc which fragments under concurrency. then cublaslt retries and falls back to GEMMEx?

mike: are we sure it's probe-time? could be shape variation mid-batch (long prefix then short) causing wrong heuristic batch coalescing.

ana: yeah, trace shows mixed sequence lengths within the same batch; our batching heuristic coalesced a long seq with several short ones (batcher config: max_tokens_per_batch=4096, pack_mining enabled). that drove the probe to try a large workspace algo.

raj: perfetto flame: I see KV cache miss spike aligned with the cudaMallocAsync windows. Eviction thrashing -> KV warmups -> extra matmul calls. So it's a compound effect: batching heuristic -> workspace overflow -> async alloc fragmentation -> kv eviction -> warmup regen -> latency tail.

perfbot: Automated check: this run (job-2026-03-16-2214) shows GC-like KV eviction rate 4x baseline and 2.4x cudaMallocAsync calls vs last week.

jun: quick mitigation ideas: 1) blacklist algo3 for shapes that exceed prealloc slab heuristics 2) reduce probe workspace cap (force smaller workspaces) 3) change batching to split long seqs into separate batches or disable pack_mining for high-variance traffic 4) pre-warm KV cache before long batches

mike: agree. also consider forcing cublasLt to use workspace workspace_policy=USE_WORKSPACE_LIMIT (we have flag) so probe won't pick >limit algos. and add allocator retry backoff to avoid repeated cudaMallocAsync on failure.

ana: i'm going to run a targeted nsys sweep with the new flag (workspace_limit=256MB) and a perfetto capture of KV events. will try both "split-mix" and "pack-disabled" batching configs. i'll post traces here.

raj: if you can reproduce on a dev GPU, we should run memprof to see fragmentation patterns too. if fragmentation is worst-case, we might need to pre-reserve a transient workspace slab for cublasLt that bypasses the general allocator.

ana: plan: (1) reproduce locally with same workload, (2) run nsys + memprof to confirm alloc fragmentation, (3) test workspace_limit and blacklist patch, (4) run canary with pack_mining disabled. target: roll to prod canary by EOD tomorrow if we have clean traces.

mike: +1 on canary. please open a quick PR and link the perf traces.

ana: opened PR #4128 with repro harness and initial nsys captures. linking here: https://stash.redwood/s/r/perf/4128 (internal). will attach perfetto slices in the PR.

jun: nice. one small test-case we should add: simulate KV concurrent evictions while probing to confirm the interaction. that will make root cause convincing for ops/eng.

ana: good call — adding a KV thrash driver to the harness now. i'll post updated traces in the PR. :thumbsup:

mike: thanks — if anyone sees this in prod meantime, turn off pack_mining on the model route to reduce risk.

ana: noted. will coordinate with oncall if we see more spikes.

(END)
